title: Emitting loop machine
statement: Let $B$ and $F$ be finite Turing machines on Boolean words, let $q$ be a state of $B$, and let $I$ be a predicate on pairs of Boolean words. Let $u$ and $v$ be functions on pairs of Boolean words, let $s_0$ be a function on Boolean words, and let $R,T : \\mathbb{N} \\to \\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $F$ computes the little-endian binary digits of $R(|x|)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps on every input $x$; $I(x,s_0(x))$ holds and $I(x,s)$ implies $I(x,u(x,s))$; and, for every $x$, the computation of $B$ from its initial configuration reaches the clean seam with state $q$ and tape word $s_0(x)$ at some time at most $T(|x|)$, without visiting $q$ earlier. Suppose also that for every $x,s$ with $I(x,s)$, the computation from the clean seam with word $s$ takes a positive number of steps at most $T(|x|)$ without an intermediate return to $q$, and ends at the clean seam with word $u(x,s)$ and output appended as $v(x,s)$. Then there are a finite Turing machine $E$ and a natural number $c$ such that $E$ computes the concatenation of $v(x,s_0(x)),v(x,u(x,s_0(x))),\\ldots,v(x,u^ {R(|x|)}(s_0(x)))$ within $c(T(n)+1)(R(n)+2)$ steps on inputs of length $n$.
hypotheses_covered: $B,F$ are finite Turing machines over Boolean words
$I$ is a predicate on pairs of Boolean words
$u,v$ are functions on pairs of Boolean words; $s_0$ is a function on Boolean words
$R,T$ map natural numbers to natural numbers
$F$ computes the binary digits of $R(|x|)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps for every $x$
For every $x$, startup reaches the clean seam with word $s_0(x)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps and does not visit $q$ earlier

For every invariant pair $(x,s)$, a round takes positive time at most $T(|x|)$, does not revisit $q$ at intermediate positive times, reaches the clean seam with word $u(x,s)$, and appends $v(x,s)$ to the output

Let a loop body with anchor be given, a fuel machine computing the binary digits of
$R(|x|)$ in time $T$, an invariant that holds at the initial word and is preserved by
the step function, a startup reaching the initial seam within $T(|x|)$ without visiting
the anchor earlier, and a per-round contract: on every admissible word $s$, in positive
time at most $T(|x|)$ with no early anchor revisit, the body moves from the clean seam
of $s$ to the clean seam of the stepped word while appending exactly the chunk word
assigned to $(x, s)$ to its output. Then there are a finite machine $E$ and a constant
$c$ such that $E$ computes, within $c (T(n) + 1)(R(n) + 2)$ steps on inputs of length
$n$, the concatenation of the chunks of the first $R(|x|) + 1$ orbit points of the
initial word, in order.
